faq.q: What is the origin of Cavid?
faq.a: Cavid is associated with Persian. Cavid is the Azerbaijani form of Persian جاوید (jāvīd), meaning 'eternal, everlasting'.
No — the underlying form is Persian, not Arabic.
Cavid can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Persian-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Cavid, cavid. Script forms are جاويد, جاوید, جَاوِيد, जाविद.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
